prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Dallas. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Dallas for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific practices — I just need one quick detail: what Dallas ZIP code or neighborhood are you in (or how far are you willing to travel)? Implant care is local, and I’ll make a short, vetted list near you.

While you reply, here’s useful guidance so you know which offices to call and why:

Which kinds of practices to call (and why)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons — best for surgical complexity (impacted teeth, large bone grafts, IV sedation, hospital privileges). Call them if you expect difficult surgery or heavy sedation needs.
- Board-certified periodontists — specialists in gums and implant placement; excellent for bone grafts, sinus lifts, and esthetic implant sites.
- Prosthodontists — specialists in designing and restoring implant crowns/bridges/full-arch prostheses; call them when you care about the final fit/occlusion/esthetic outcome (especially full-arch or multiple-tooth rehab).
- Full-service implant centers (team of surgeon + restorative dentist + in‑house lab) — convenient for coordinated care, guided surgery, same-day provisional restorations.
- Dental school or university clinics (if available) — lower cost option with supervised specialists; good for straightforward cases if budget is a concern.

What to ask each office (script you can use)
1. “Do you place and restore implants, and who will be doing each part?” (surgeon vs restorative dentist)
2. “Are you board-certified in your specialty?” (oral surgeon/periodontist/prosthodontist)
3. “Do you use CBCT 3D imaging and guided implant planning?” (important for accuracy)
4. “What implant systems/brands do you use?” (Nobel, Straumann, BioHorizons, etc. — reputable brands)
5. “Will I need bone grafting or a sinus lift, and how does that affect treatment time?” 
6. “Do you offer sedation or IV anesthesia?” (if nervous or complex surgery)
7. “What is the full estimated cost, and what’s included (surgery, implant, abutment, crown, follow‑ups)?” 
8. “Do you finance or accept my insurance, and do you provide a written treatment plan?” 
9. “Can I see before/after photos and patient references for similar cases?” 
10. “What’s the expected timeline from placement to final crown?”

Red flags to avoid
- Vague answers on who restores the implant (the surgeon should coordinate with a dentist/prosthodontist).
- No CBCT available for implant planning.
- Extremely low price without clear explanation (may use poor-quality components or skip steps).
- No written treatment plan or breakdown of costs.

What to expect in price & timeline (ballpark)
- Single implant (surgery + implant + abutment + crown): typically in the $3,000–6,000 range in the Dallas area depending on complexity and materials.
- Bone grafting or sinus lift adds cost and time (3–6+ months healing).
- Same-day teeth/All‑on‑4 are available at many centers but are more expensive and require careful case selection.

If you want, give me:
- your ZIP code or neighborhood, and
- whether this is a single tooth, multiple teeth, or full-arch replacement, and
- any preference for sedation or price constraints

I’ll return a short list (3–6) of Dallas-area practices to call, with a one-line reason for each (e.g., oral surgeon for complex cases, restorative-driven implant practice for esthetics), plus phone/script suggestions tailored to each.
